en: Josh is founder and CEO of Mecca AI, which is building a data and deployment company for robotics.

speaker: Unknown
en: I, and I think the whole ecosystem think that robotics is about to enter a golden age.

speaker: Unknown
en: And unlike LLMs where we had so much free human data from the internet, robotics is fundamentally data constrained.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think...

speaker: Unknown
en: Your position in the ecosystem as the leading data factory to bring robotic data and physical data in distribution for models is just a really, really interesting perch.
zh: 你在生态系统中的位置，作为领先的数据工厂，把机器人数据和物理数据带入模型的分布中，是一个非常非常有趣的观察点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm excited to use this conversation today to chat about how does egocentric data and data collection work in robotics, what are the actual operations and economics of operating a data factory, and your overall thoughts on robotics research and deployment.
zh: 所以我很期待用今天的对话聊聊：自我中心数据在机器人技术中如何运作、数据采集如何运作，运营一家数据工厂的实际运营和经济状况，以及你对机器人研究和部署的总体看法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thanks for joining the show.
zh: 感谢你参加节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Amazing.

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Awesome.

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe to start off, for those who aren't familiar, what is Mecca and how are you looking to impact the world of robotics?
zh: 也许先从那些不熟悉的人说起，Mecca 是什么，你希望如何影响机器人技术的世界？

speaker: Unknown
en: So Mecca is, like you said, the data and deployment company for Physically High.
zh: Mecca 就像你说的，是物理 AI 的数据和部署公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: What that means is today we create, we process, and ultimately we license a lot of the data that goes into training these robotics foundation models.
zh: 这意味着今天我们创建、处理，并最终授权许可大量用于训练这些机器人基础模型的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: The big problem across robotics is that we don't have the luxury of the cold start that LLMs had with the internet.
zh: 机器人技术领域的大问题在于，我们没有 LLM 曾有的互联网那样的冷启动的奢侈条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fundamentally, a lot of this robotics data is three things.
zh: 从根本上说，这些机器人数据主要是三样东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's pixels, it's actions, and it's logic.
zh: 它是像素，是动作，是逻辑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we don't have access to a large amount of this curated and processed and clean data to be able to then train these models to understand what it is to be in the physical world.
zh: 所以我们无法获得大量这种经过整理、处理和清洗的数据，来训练这些模型理解身处物理世界意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of our job is pretty much to, one, create the different types of hardware, such as sensorizing and wearables for humans, the different operations to go and collect and partner with individual contributors, businesses, tasks across different environments, and then ultimately post-process and own the quality gates.
zh: 所以我们的很多工作基本上是：一，创建不同类型的硬件，比如为人类加装传感器的设备和可穿戴设备，不同的运营方式去与个人贡献者、企业、不同环境中的任务合作并采集数据，然后最终进行后处理并把控质量门。

speaker: Unknown
en: to make these datasets useful and teach robots about the world.
zh: 使这些数据集变得有用，教会机器人了解世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Without having been given the benefits of a giant, free, many trillions of tokens, maybe lots of trillions, trillions of trillions of tokens of internet corpus, do you think that robotics, having to pay for and operationally collect all the data that's going into the mix, is it even a feasible challenge?
zh: 在没有得到一个巨大的、免费的、可能有数万亿、数万亿乘数万亿 token 的互联网语料库的好处的情况下，你认为机器人技术必须付费并靠运营采集所有进入混合的数据，这甚至是一个可行的挑战吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it economically feasible without having had the gift of the internet?
zh: 在没有得到互联网这份礼物的情况下，这在经济上可行吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we still have the luxury of a lot of things that was given from the internet.
zh: 我认为我们仍然拥有从互联网那里继承来的很多东西的奢侈条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we aren't starting from zero, ultimately.
zh: 所以我们从根本上并不是从零开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you can see it across LLMs and data across LLMs.
zh: 我认为你可以在 LLM 及其数据上看到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretraining data was always driven by the labs, largely, across web crawlers, things like that.
zh: 预训练数据一直主要由实验室推动，主要通过网络爬虫之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It didn't become a large market.
zh: 它并没有成为一个大市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today in robotics, we do see pretraining as quite a large market.
zh: 今天在机器人技术领域，我们确实看到预训练是一个相当大的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that could be taken in several forms.
zh: 而且这可以以几种形式呈现。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that could be that we are teaching video models how to generate more physics-grounded realities of what the world looks like.
zh: 比如我们正在教视频模型如何生成更贴近物理规律的世界景象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we get to leverage all the work that has gone into the VLMs and then different types of world models before to make that possible.
zh: 而且我们可以利用之前在 VLM 以及不同类型的世界模型上所做的所有工作来实现这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it possible and scalable to get to that volume of data?
zh: 要达到那样的数据量是可能的、可扩展的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that ultimately comes down to what commercial use case can you unlock at which levels of scales of data?
zh: 我认为这最终归结为：在哪个数据规模层级上，你能解锁什么样的商业用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our strong belief is along that journey that we will be able to unlock a lot of the simple pick-and-place tasks along the beginning of what we're creating.
zh: 而我们坚定的信念是，在这一路上，我们将能够在初期解锁很多简单的抓取放置任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And towards that long tail, that is going to be many orders of magnitudes larger than it is today.
zh: 而朝着那个长尾前进，那将会比今天大许多个数量级。

en: And so I think in the same vein for us, that is the human brain runs on just 20 watts.

en: Love that.

en: You come from an untraditional background for robotics.
zh: 你的背景在机器人领域算是非传统的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you started in the fintech world and the sneaker world.
zh: 我记得你是从金融科技领域和球鞋领域起步的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I'm not mistaken, tell me about how you and your co-founder found your way to robotics.
zh: 如果我没记错的话,跟我讲讲你和你联合创始人是怎么走到机器人这条路上来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was quite an interesting journey.
zh: 这是一段相当有意思的旅程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a big part of what brought us together, one, we're both Canadian, and two, is we have this big science fiction grounding.
zh: 而且我认为把我们聚在一起的重要原因,一是我们都是加拿大人,二是我们都有深厚的科幻底子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the belief ultimately was that payment was a hard and difficult problem, but whatever we worked on next, we wanted to be something that seemed exciting that the future was going to be incredible.
zh: 所以最终我们的信念是,支付是一个困难的问题,但我们接下来想做的,应该是某种看起来令人兴奋、未来会非常了不起的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And robotics seemed like a great space to get into.
zh: 而机器人看起来是一个很值得进入的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember walking into your office and then immediately seeing those like mechatronic robots and then the Kawasaki Corleos on the wall.
zh: 我记得走进你们办公室,立刻就看到那些机电一体化机器人,还有墙上挂的川崎 Corleos。

speaker: Unknown
en: The inner child in you must be very happy about what you're doing these days.
zh: 你内心的那个孩子现在对你做的事情一定非常开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 是的,绝对是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coming from a non-robotics background, what do you think your advantages are in building this business?

speaker: Unknown
en: And where has it presented challenges?
zh: 又在哪些方面带来了挑战?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the advantages is when we entered the space, we had to go and do this full discovery process.
zh: 我认为优势在于,当我们进入这个领域时,我们得去做这个完整的探索过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We reached out to hundreds of folks that were in the space that we appreciated.

speaker: Unknown
en: We read every paper that we get our hands on.

speaker: Unknown
en: We went to visit the different robot labs.

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we saw in late 24, roughly, GPT was taking off.
zh: 而且在大约 24 年底,我们所看到的是 GPT 正在腾飞。

speaker: Unknown
en: Robotics was still evolving from this traditional robotics era.
zh: 机器人还在从传统机器人时代演进。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it seems obvious to us at the very least that data and compute would become very important across the industry.
zh: 至少对我们来说,数据和算力将在整个行业中变得非常重要,这一点似乎显而易见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so moving towards that, we got to read and see some of the papers like Ego4D from a fresh lens and say, hey, there's about 4,000 hours of this human demonstration data.
zh: 朝着这个方向,我们得以用全新的视角去阅读和看到一些论文,比如 Ego4D,然后说,嘿,这里大约有 4000 小时的人类示范数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you actually went in to look at the data, you would realize some of the data sets would be daily life of folks like bowling, for example.
zh: 当你真正深入去看这些数据,你会发现有些数据集是人们的日常生活,比如打保龄球。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was very broad use cases and potential applications at the 4,000-hour scale.
zh: 在 4000 小时的规模上,存在着非常广泛的用例和潜在应用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so coming into that with a fresh lens, we were able to, from the first principles approach, I'd say, have a general intuition of what would be important and then iterate very closely with people that were much smarter than us that had different views of what the future would be and be able to stay close to iterate on what the product would become.
zh: 所以带着全新的视角进来,我们能够,我想说,用第一性原理的方法,对什么会是重要的形成一个大致的直觉,然后与那些比我们聪明得多、对未来有不同看法的人紧密迭代,并保持贴近去迭代产品会变成什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, interesting.
zh: 是的,有意思。

en: It seems like robotics has just changed so quickly as a field that almost coming from the field can be an advantage and a disadvantage because people come from different eras of what's important in the training mix and things like that.

zh: 而且我记得你创建公司时,基本上就是在它背后下注。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 显然,现在这个已经分布得广多了,但什么是自我中心数据?

en: Egocentric data is pretty much video data from humans demonstrating and doing tasks from a first person POV.
zh: 自我中心数据基本上就是人类以第一人称视角展示和执行任务的视频数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: The high level idea was that from the gap of human data to robotics data, you could close a lot of the vision gap.
zh: 高层次的想法是,从人类数据到机器人数据的鸿沟之间,你可以弥合很大一部分视觉差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: Where robotics experience the world from POV, can we also show it what it is like to interact with the world from first person as well?
zh: 机器人以第一人称视角体验世界,那我们是否也能让它看到以第一人称与世界互动是什么样子?

speaker: Unknown
en: Why we bet on it was pretty much when we explored the space.
zh: 我们为什么押注它,基本上是当我们探索这个领域时。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of what we saw was robotics data at the time was teleoperation, which was humans controlling robots to do demonstrations.
zh: 我们当时看到的大量机器人数据是遥操作,也就是人类控制机器人去做演示。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was very hard to scale at the time.
zh: 那在当时非常难以规模化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And from what we saw across GPT and a lot of the principles of scaling up, we had to find ways to scale up data much more significantly.
zh: 而且基于我们在 GPT 身上以及很多规模化原则中看到的,我们得找到能更大规模地扩展数据的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think some of our early intuitions were that
zh: 我认为我们早期的一些直觉是

en: Humans and robots share a lot of similarities.

speaker: Unknown
en: Humanoids were just starting to take off.
zh: 人形机器人当时才刚刚开始起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Humans and humanoids look the same.

en: And so what does that look like?

zh: 我们让中国的阿姨和叔叔们录下自己做饭、打扫、做各种任务的过程。

speaker: Unknown

en: We tried a number of things.

en: And that's evolved quite a bit into all the custom hardware that we have to produce now and all the different partnerships that we have to have across different industries.

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, we're sensorizing humans, and that's the broader category.
zh: 说到底，我们是在给人类加装传感器，这是更广义的类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: How important is it to get forced data from the sensors?
zh: 从传感器获取力数据有多重要？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because one of the things I've always thought about is in self-driving, you don't really need forced data as much, right?
zh: 因为我一直在想的一点是，在自动驾驶里，你其实不太需要力数据，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas with robotics, especially with manipulation, you really care about how hard am I squeezing that door handle or picking up that egg?
zh: 而在机器人领域，尤其是操控方面，你真的很在乎我拧那个门把手或者拿起那个鸡蛋时用了多大力？

en: And it seems to me that video doesn't quite capture that.

en: You might be able to approximate it but doesn't really capture it.
zh: 你也许能近似地估算，但它并不能真正捕捉到。

en: How important is capturing force data and how do you think about getting that?
